scope: turn the four dogfood defects into a gate: a rules audit plus a dogfood test
why: four packages shipped rules that had only ever been observed firing. Every unit test passed. What found them was pointing the checker at real work, so the corpus became a test.

gate1_rulesAudit.requirement: every rule must be observed in both directions: a bad document makes it fire, a valid document leaves it silent
gate1_rulesAudit.definitionOfSilent: either a negated per-rule assertion, or a package-level test proving a valid document produces zero errors

deadRulesFound.why: HEADER required .+ after the colon, so 'feat:' never parsed and the rule was unreachable
pick() deliberately skips empty values, so a present-but-empty SKU cell was reported as sku-missing
deadRulesFound.fix: new columnName() answers 'is the column there', separate from 'what is in it'

gate1_rulesAudit.alsoAdded: 13 firing tests for rules that had only a silent-direction test (agreement 3, listing 4, invoice 2, bug-report/env-example/dockerfile/commit-msg 1 each)

asserts: 22 READMEs pass onboarding-check with zero errors and zero warnings
120 real commits raise no type-prefix error — the history is not Conventional Commits and must not be blocked for it
gate2_dogfood.vacuousnessGuard: corpus size asserted first, so the test cannot pass on an empty file list
gate2_dogfood.firstCatch: dsh-review-outbox/README.md had no help path; a 遇到问题 section was added

lesson: a rule tested only in the direction that fires is half a rule. The half that is usually missing is the one that says 'and here is a document that is fine, and I leave it alone' — which is the half that decides whether a stranger keeps the tool installed.
